Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Valid application is not authenticated and authorised to access data for which they have permission.
Cause: Error requesting access token e.g. error in the payload or header
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation uses Supabase-managed JWT generation for application-restricted access. Token requests are handled server-side in the nhs-pds-lookup Edge Function using NHS_PDS_API_KEY env var. Error responses from the NHS token endpoint are caught and returned as explicit errors to the caller.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Token request handled entirely server-side in nhs-pds-lookup Edge Function. NHS_PDS_API_KEY stored as Supabase secret — never exposed to client. Token errors caught with explicit error handling; pharmacist sees a clear 'PDS authentication failed' message. All auth failures logged to ps_audit_log with timestamp and user_id.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Valid application is not authenticated and authorised to access data for which they have permission.
Cause: Error generating and signing the JWT
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: JWT generation uses the NHS-specified signed JWT pattern. Signing is performed server-side using the private key stored in Supabase secrets. Key rotation process documented in ISMS credential management procedure.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: JWT signed server-side using private key stored in Supabase Edge Function secrets (not in code or client). JWT generation errors caught and logged. Key material never transmitted to client. Annual key rotation included in ISMS review schedule.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Valid application is not authenticated and authorised to access data for which they have permission.
Cause: Valid but incorrect token sent by connecting system
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: nhs-pds-lookup constructs the PDS API request headers programmatically from the stored key material. The token used is the one returned from the NHS token endpoint for that request — no manual token handling possible.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Token constructed and injected into PDS request headers entirely by server-side Edge Function code. No user or client input can affect the token value. 401/403 responses from PDS are caught and returned as explicit auth error messages with logging.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: A request to patient or related person end points is rejected
Cause: The SEARCH or GET patient request is rejected by the PDS API Proxy because there is a problem with the token sent by the calling system (invalid or missing or expired)
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Access tokens are requested fresh for each PDS API call in sandbox/INT mode. Token expiry is not cached — each invocation of nhs-pds-lookup acquires a valid token before making the PDS request.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Token acquired per-request before each PDS call. 401 responses from PDS proxy trigger an explicit 'PDS authentication failed — please retry' error surfaced to the pharmacist. All rejections logged with HTTP status and error body in ps_audit_log for support investigation.

Risk Grouping: Patient Search / Retrieve / Related Persons - No Match
Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: SEARCH patient, GET patient or GET related person request returns no match from PDS
Cause: The connecting system is not compliant to the API specification i.e. structure incorrect data correct
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: nhs-pds-lookup constructs PDS FHIR R4 requests strictly per the NHS PDS FHIR API specification. URL patterns use /Patient/{nhsNumber} for GET and /Patient?{params} for search. Accept header set to application/fhir+json. Request construction is unit-tested against the PDS sandbox.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Request construction follows PDS FHIR R4 spec. Tested against PDS sandbox (open access) — lookup and search actions verified. NHS number Mod-11 validation server-side prevents structurally invalid NHS numbers reaching PDS. Accept: application/fhir+json header set on all requests.

Risk Grouping: Patient Search / Retrieve / Related Persons - No Match
Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: SEARCH patient, GET patient or GET related person request returns no match from PDS
Cause: Incorrect data sent by connecting system i.e. structure correct data incorrect
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: NHS number is validated server-side with Mod-11 check before any PDS request. Search parameters (family name mandatory) validated before constructing search URL. No-match responses (empty Bundle) returned to pharmacist with clear 'Patient not found' message.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Server-side NHS number Mod-11 validation in validateNHSNumber() — returns 400 INVALID_NHS_NUMBER before calling PDS if check fails. Search requires at minimum family name. PDS 404 / empty Bundle returned as clear 'Patient not found in PDS' message to pharmacist. All no-match outcomes logged.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: SEARCH patient request returns no match from PDS
Cause: Incorrect setting of wildcard flag by connecting system
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation does not manipulate wildcard settings in PDS search requests. All search parameter values are passed as provided by the pharmacist. Wildcard behaviour is governed entirely by PDS.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: No wildcard flag manipulation by Pharmstation. Search parameters passed as-is to PDS FHIR search URL. Wildcard handling is PDS-native. Pharmacist-entered values are not modified before submission.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: SEARCH patient request returns no match from PDS
Cause: Incorrect setting of special characters by connecting system
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Search parameter values are URL-encoded using URLSearchParams before being appended to the PDS search URL. Special characters cannot cause malformed requests.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: All search parameters URL-encoded via JavaScript URLSearchParams in nhs-pds-lookup handleSearch(). Special characters in patient names (e.g. O'Brien, García) are correctly encoded before transmission. Tested in sandbox with non-ASCII name characters.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: System displays incorrect or incomplete details for the patient
Cause: For connecting system using the GET request to patient or related person it sends incorrect NHS No.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: NHS number entered by pharmacist is validated server-side (Mod-11 check) before being used in GET /Patient/{nhsNumber}. Returned patient details (name, DOB, address) are displayed to pharmacist for mandatory confirmation before any service or claim proceeds.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Server-side Mod-11 NHS number validation. Mandatory patient confirmation step — pharmacist must confirm displayed name + DOB + address before proceeding. Confirmation logged in ps_audit_log with user_id and timestamp. Cache stores verified NHS number only after confirmation.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: System displays incorrect or incomplete details for the patient
Cause: Connecting system fails to correctly process response from PDS API (System level)
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: parseFHIRPatient() in nhs-pds-lookup parses the FHIR R4 Patient resource into Pharmstation's internal format. All fields use safe null-coalescing — missing optional fields return null rather than crashing. Full raw PDS response stored in full_pds_response column for audit.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: FHIR Patient resource parsed by parseFHIRPatient() with null-safe field extraction. Missing fields return null — no crash on partial responses. Full raw PDS response stored in ps_nhs_patient_pds_cache.full_pds_response for audit comparison. Parse errors caught and logged.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: System displays incorrect or incomplete details for the patient
Cause: Connecting system fails to correctly present the data returned from PDS API (Presentation layer)
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation UI uses TypeScript typed interfaces for PDS patient data. All demographic fields rendered with explicit null handling — missing fields shown as 'Not recorded' rather than blank or wrong value. UI display tested against PDS sandbox responses.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: TypeScript typed interfaces for PDS Patient data. UI renders all returned fields with explicit null/undefined handling. Missing optional fields displayed as 'Not recorded'. Pharmacist confirmation screen shows all key fields before proceeding. UI tested against PDS sandbox canned test patients.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: An out of date NHS No. is used in correspondence
Cause: The superseded NHS No. returned in a retrieval is not handled by the connecting system
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: PDS returns superseded NHS number indication in the response. Pharmstation's handleLookup() will be updated to detect this, warn the pharmacist, and replace the local record with the superseding NHS number where no conflict exists. This is tracked as a P1 item in the pre-go-live engineering checklist.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Superseded NHS number detection is a P1 item in Pharmstation's pre-go-live engineering checklist (documentation/technical/pre-golive-engineering-checklist.md). Implementation: detect superseded response from PDS, display warning to pharmacist (NHS number replaced; inform patient), replace local cache record with superseding number if no conflict. Scheduled for completion before witness testing.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Location based data for a sensitive patient held on the local record is shared with an unauthorised user
Cause: The connecting system does not recognise and act upon sensitive patient indicator returned to suppress patient locality and other sensitive details held in the local patient record
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: pds_restricted boolean is stored in ps_nhs_patient_pds_cache and returned from nhs-pds-lookup. UI sensitive patient warning banner and location field suppression are P1 items in the pre-go-live engineering checklist. Until implemented, sensitive flag triggers a system-level block preventing service delivery from proceeding.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: pds_restricted flag stored and returned from nhs-pds-lookup. Sensitive patient UI warning (banner + location field suppression + RBAC restriction) is a P1 item in pre-go-live engineering checklist. Scheduled for completion before witness testing. Interim control: sensitive flag returned to UI; location fields not displayed until warning acknowledged.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The external system displays the wrong error message such that the user is unable to determine the next activity correctly
Cause: A fault in the connecting system results in wrong message being displayed
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: nhs-pds-lookup returns structured JSON error responses with specific error codes (PATIENT_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_NHS_NUMBER, PDS_AUTH_ERROR etc.) and human-readable messages with actionable next steps. UI maps each error code to a specific user-facing message.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Structured error responses with machine-readable codes and human-readable messages. Each PDS error code maps to a specific user action: PATIENT_NOT_FOUND → 'Patient not found — check NHS number and retry'; PDS_UNAVAILABLE → 'PDS temporarily unavailable — verify patient manually from ID'; PDS_AUTH_ERROR → 'Contact system administrator'. All errors logged.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The system does not allow the user to provide patient care
Cause: Synchronisation failure prevents the connecting system from using the patient record for a care episode
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: If PDS is unavailable, nhs-pds-lookup returns a PDS_UNAVAILABLE error with HTTP 503. The UI displays a clear warning and allows the pharmacist to continue with manually verified patient demographics. Care is not blocked by PDS unavailability.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: PDS_UNAVAILABLE error (503) triggers a UI fallback mode: pharmacist sees 'PDS unavailable — verify patient identity manually from photo ID before continuing'. Manual demographic entry fields are fully editable. Service delivery can continue. Fallback usage is logged in ps_audit_log for post-incident review.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Up to date information held on the local system is overwritten by older/out of date information from PDS
Cause: The connecting system does not use versionId or other mechanism to detect differences between local and PDS data and therefore does not alert the user that there are differences
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: On re-sync (lookup of a cached patient), Pharmstation will compare returned PDS data against cached values for key field changes. Key field change detection and pharmacist notification is a P1 item in the pre-go-live engineering checklist.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Key field change detection on re-sync is a P1 item in pre-go-live engineering checklist. Implementation: compare PDS response key fields (name, DOB, death status, gender) against cached values; if changed, display notification to pharmacist before updating cache. Pharmacist must confirm before cache is updated. versionId stored alongside cached record.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: Unable to identify user initiated actions relating to the PDS FHIR API
Cause: Where the end user is a healthcare worker or patient, the connecting system is not locally authenticating the end user and auditing their actions
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: All PDS lookups require a valid Supabase JWT from the authenticated pharmacist. The user_id from the JWT is logged in ps_audit_log alongside org_id, action, NHS number queried, and timestamp. Unauthenticated requests are rejected before reaching PDS.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Every nhs-pds-lookup call requires valid Supabase Auth JWT. user_id extracted from JWT and logged in ps_audit_log with: action (lookup/search/verify), org_id, nhs_number queried, http_status, timestamp. Append-only audit table — no DELETE permission. Audit write is transactionally coupled to PDS response processing.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: End user experiencing performance issues that are serious enough to render the system unusable
Cause: Performance issues with the system (e.g. not sized correctly bad coding)
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: nhs-pds-lookup runs on Supabase Edge Functions (Deno Deploy, global edge network). PDS sandbox response times are typically under 500ms. 24-hour cache reduces PDS calls for repeat lookups. Rate limit (5 TPS default) is not approached at pilot scale.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: Edge Functions on Deno Deploy (global edge) — low latency to NHS API endpoints. 24-hour cache reduces repeat PDS calls. Async/await non-blocking. PDS response time monitored via Supabase dashboard. Pilot scale (1-5 pharmacies) generates well under 5 TPS. Performance regression alerts via Vercel/Supabase monitoring.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: System is unavailable
Cause: The solution is not resilient: Resilience/Failover, single points of failure, load balancing, Backup and Recovery, Disaster Recovery
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Supabase Edge Functions deployed on Deno Deploy (global multi-region). Vercel frontend is globally distributed CDN. Both have 99.9%+ SLA. PDS unavailability handled gracefully via fallback mode. Supabase daily automated backups. Vercel instant rollback on deployment failure.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Supabase global edge deployment — no single regional point of failure. (2) Vercel global CDN. (3) PDS_UNAVAILABLE fallback mode allows care to continue. (4) Supabase daily automated backups. (5) Vercel instant rollback. (6) Status monitoring via Supabase and Vercel status pages. (7) Deputy CSO appointed for continuity.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The system is experiencing problems but the user has no visibility of this.
Cause: Alerting and monitoring is either not present or not fit for purpose.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Vercel 'Failed Deployment' notifications and Supabase 'Failed function deploy' alerts configured to CSO email. PDS errors surfaced to end users with explicit error messages — never silent failures. All PDS call outcomes logged in ps_audit_log for CSO monthly review.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Vercel Failed Deployment → CSO email alert. (2) Supabase Failed function deploy → CSO email alert. (3) All PDS errors surfaced to user with visible message — no silent failures. (4) ps_audit_log records all PDS call outcomes for monthly CSO review. (5) Admin panel surfaces PDS error rates.

Unwanted Effect/Outcome Description: The system has not deployed correctly
Cause: Poor transition / deployment plans.
Justification of Cause Likelihood Rating: Pharmstation uses CI/CD via Vercel (frontend) and Supabase CLI (Edge Functions). Post-deployment smoke test includes a PDS sandbox lookup call to confirm nhs-pds-lookup is live and responding. Release checklist signed off by CSO before production deployment.
Supplier Internal Mitigations: (1) Vercel atomic deployments with instant rollback. (2) Supabase Edge Function deployment via CLI with version tracking. (3) Post-deployment smoke test: PDS sandbox lookup confirms function is live. (4) Build failure alerts to CSO. (5) Release checklist signed off by CSO (Champe Chilufya GPhC 2226350) before each production deployment.
